articles.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange strikes a day before U.S.-brokered talks are scheduled to begin
articles.summary: President Donald Trump mentioned in a "60 Minutes" interview that the two sides are "very close" to a deal.
articles.body: KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russia battered Ukraine's power grid again and Ukrainian forces hit another of Russia's biggest oil refineries, officials said Monday, hours before delegations from Moscow and Kyiv were due to meet for new U.S.-brokered talks on how to end the fighting. Nearly five years after Russia invaded its neighbor, the two countries remain locked in battle with no sign that either side is ready to budge from their demands. The war has already killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians, analysts and humanitarian organizations say. The three-way talks between envoys from the U.S., Russia and Ukraine are due to start in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, on Tuesday and last for two days. The previous round of talks was in February. U.S. President Donald Trump said in a "60 Minutes" interview that aired Sunday that Moscow and Kyiv are "very close" to a deal, despite the "tremendous hatred" between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. He said that Ukraine would have "a little bit different shape" under the settlement, but he didn't elaborate. Trump has previously made statements about developments in the war which haven't materialized. Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, who will mediate in the talks with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, said that the priorities will be ending the conflict, finding ways to stop the war reigniting, reviving Ukraine's postwar economy and preparing humanitarian aid. "We hope these discussions will identify areas of common ground, advance practical solutions, and build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations," Kushner said on X Monday. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Monday that Trump's team has placed "collective security," covering not just Russia and Ukraine but also a wider area, at the top of the agenda. The last three-way talks, in Geneva nine months ago, also took place amid continuing attacks. They delivered no significant progress in ending the war, but some circumstances have changed. Trump, whose stance on the war has varied, has to reckon with Democrats taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections. They could demand more support for Ukraine. Russian state finances are under heavy strain because of the war, and Ukraine's economy is being choked by the relentless attacks. In Abu Dhabi, the talks will look at what security guarantees would satisfy Russia, which sees NATO as a threat, and Ukraine, which wants to prevent future Russian invasions. Putin has sought to sideline European countries and negotiate Ukraine's future directly with Trump. However, European leaders and Ukraine have insisted that they be included. Moscow says that European representatives won't be directly involved in the Abu Dhabi discussions, but European officials said that representatives will be in the United Arab Emirates. Ukraine's lead negotiator, Rustem Umerov, said that European officials will hold "separate coordination" with the delegation from Kyiv. Kushner said that before the talks in Abu Dhabi begin, he and Witkoff will consult with officials from Ukraine, the European Union, NATO, Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Italy. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Monday that the meeting would focus on trilateral negotiations, with the United States mediating between Russia and Ukraine. "You are aware that the Americans have their own channels of communication with the Europeans, as do the Ukrainians, and it appears they are already establishing their own methods of coordination," Peskov said. "But, to reiterate, this is a matter of trilateral negotiations." Russian forces targeted four electrical substations in Ukraine's Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Cherkasy and Vinnytsia regions, Russia's Defense Ministry said Monday. The attacks are part of Russia's campaign to deny Ukrainian civilians heating, light and running water during the approaching winter. Zelenskyy said Monday that the European Union had agreed to activate a special emergency mechanism that speeds up funding for power grid repairs. Russia launched 317 drones of various types including 105 jet-powered drones at Ukraine overnight, Ukraine's air force said. Russian aerial attacks have pummeled Ukraine throughout the war, with gruesome consequences. A Russian glide bomb attack last week near the front line in the southern Zaporizhzhia region killed at least 55 people at an aid distribution center. On Monday, Russian forces hit a warehouse in Odesa in southwestern Ukraine containing food supplies for kindergartens and schools, killing three people, local officials said. Meanwhile, an attack by long-range drones developed by Ukraine during the war started a fire at the KINEF oil refinery, one of Russia's largest, close to St. Petersburg and more than 1,200 kilometers (745 miles) from the Ukrainian border, Leningrad Gov. Alexander Drozdenko said Monday. Ukraine said in early October that its long-range strikes had neutralized more than half of Russia's oil refining capacity, hampering Moscow's ability to supply its forces. Ukrainian forces also struck a plant near St. Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, that produces solid rocket propellant for Russia's Iskander-M ballistic missiles, Ukraine's General Staff said. Ukraine is trying to prevent Russia from firing ballistic missiles, which Kyiv's forces can't stop once they are in the air without more U.S.-made Patriot air defense systems. Patriot missiles, however, are in short supply.

Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.summary: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
articles.body: "He's suffering": Trump answers BBC question about Nvidia's Jensen Huang US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy. Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign. "I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Speaking later at a White House press briefing, Trump told reporters, "I know the FBI is looking into" the affair but did not give further details on the investigation, or confirm when it was launched. Trump added he thought that Huang was an "honourable guy and I feel very confident that he will be in good shape" after the investigations. Nvidia, which has commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company after Apple, and designs computer chips that have become central to AI technology. The revelations knocked about $250bn (£190bn) off Nvidia's value on Monday as the company's share price fell by more than 4%. US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang , also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. She is not related to Jensen Huang. According to the newspaper, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring this year, warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia. Trump's remarks are the first indication of whether Nvidia's Huang knew about the woman's alleged ties to Chinese espionage. Megaspeed's office in Singapore's central business district appeared to be operational and staffed on Tuesday. The BBC was refused entry to its floor, but spoke to a staff member by phone who said they had no comment and directed all queries to the company's PR team. Nvidia, co-founded by Jensen Huang, is also a major focus in the AI technology race between the US and China, with officials in Washington treating its exports to Beijing as a matter of national security - a key reason why Huang's affair has sparked concerns. Also on Monday, Huang and Nvidia were sued in a proposed class action lawsuit in California that accuses them of defrauding shareholders by concealing his ties with the suspected Chinese spy. The lawsuit alleges that the company lied to the media about Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, "who is suspected of seeking to help smuggle Nvidia products to China." At the White House, Trump was asked several times when he was made aware of the relationship. He said he was informed "over a period of time" but was not specific. "I hope there's no problem, I believe he is suffering greatly," the president added. He said he spoke to Huang on the phone on Monday "just to see if he's feeling alright, how you doing and I asked him about that and he said he absolutely had no idea that the person in question was a spy". Trump has raised concerns that allowing China to lead in AI would supercharge Beijing's military and surveillance capabilities. The president added he was "sure" Chinese leader Xi Jinping would "ask me about it" when they next met. Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation? Huang has admitted that he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He said on Monday that he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation the company had launched. Huang has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week, however it is unclear whether Huang will appear. A letter said the briefing would be "on Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People's Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang". Nvidia has declined to comment, while the the BBC has also contacted the committees. Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond Some workers the BBC spoke to at Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters on Monday said it was business as usual, despite the intense attention on the company. Nvidia has been around for decades, with Huang founding it with two other engineers in 1993, but its rise to one of the world's most valuable and powerful companies has only been recent. It originally designed computer chips for gaming, but its decision to shift focus to AI development turned it into the powerhouse it is today. Its chips have become so valuable to the AI buildout that the White House previously imposed controls on where its advanced products could be sold. The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US. But Huang has long been against restricting sales to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology. In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions. Nvidia's most advanced AI semiconductors including the GB200 Blackwell super chip remain blocked from the Chinese market. What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

Moldovan foreign affairs minister says constitutional neutrality must not be impediment to strengthening country’s defense capabilities
articles.summary: Moldovan foreign affairs minister says constitutional neutrality must not be impediment to strengthening country’s defense capabilities The constitutional neutrality must not be an impediment to strengthening the country’s defense capabilities. Moldova must make use of opportunities for cooperation with the European Union in the field of security.
articles.body: Moldovan foreign affairs minister says constitutional neutrality must not be impediment to strengthening country’s defense capabilities The constitutional neutrality must not be an impediment to strengthening the country’s defense capabilities. Moldova must make use of opportunities for cooperation with the European Union in the field of security. In recent years, the support provided through the European Peace Facility (EPF) has increased from 7 million euros in 2021 to 120 million euros in 2026. Deputy Prime Minister, Foreign Affairs Minister Mihai Popsoi has made statements to this effect during the annual conference on European Union enlargement, held today in Chisinau. According to the official, in recent years, the EPF has provided transformational support to the security and defense sector. “The amounts granted are colossal for the defense budget of Moldova, a sector that was neglected for decades. Given the horrors Ukraine has been going through for almost five years and their repercussions on the entire region, we must understand that a neutral country must invest more in its own defense than other states that have the peace, security and luxury of belonging to a collective defense alliance. Within the great European family, security cooperation, the strengthening of the defense industry and the development of logistical networks are mechanisms that Moldova wants to be part of. We must understand that neutrality does not mean being incapable of defending yourself. Nor does it represent an obstacle to strengthening defense capabilities and making investments in the field of defense, which we are making and will continue to make,” Mihai Popsoi said. The minister emphasized that, in addition to the EPF, the European Union also supported programmes in the civilian sector, which play an important role in strengthening societal security. “I am referring to the European Union Partnership Mission in Moldova. This mission has helped us enormously to strengthen our capabilities in the field of information security and crisis management. The Crisis Management Center and the strengthening of its capabilities are part of our accession commitments. Therefore, the existing cooperation mechanism, which is continuously developing, represents a major opportunity for Moldova to strengthen its defense and security sector, as well as society’s resilience as a whole. A state can succeed, only if every citizen and institution contributes to defending society against foreign interference. Our citizens have become aware of the danger to which we are exposed and, every time, we have proved our ability to defend our democratic choices, our right to choose our own destiny and to continue efforts to enhance the resilience of our society. This undoubtedly demonstrates our internal capacity to respond to these challenges, but it is also the result of substantial EU support,” Mihai Popsoi added. For his part, Stanislav Secrieru, the president’s chief adviser on defense and national security, noted that, under the UN Charter, every independent and sovereign state has the right to self-defense; however, in order to exercise this right, it must have the necessary means. “At present, we notice that, in the European Union, some states are investing in defense and increasing their military budgets. At the same time, neutral countries also contribute to the EPF, from which Moldova benefits through defense resources. Therefore, being neutral does not mean being passive, indifferent or failing to take care of one’s own defense capabilities. Threats in the air domain are evolving every two or three weeks. Modernizing airspace surveillance capabilities is a lengthy process, as drones flying at low altitudes require specialized radars. Moreover, even if Moldova had the financial resources, the delivery of equipment would not be immediate, as manufacturers are prioritizing orders for Ukraine, where the situation is more serious. Another challenge concerns training and retaining in service specialists capable of operating increasingly sophisticated equipment,” Stanislav Secrieru said. A 120-million-euros-worth assistance package is being provided by the European Union through the European Peace Facility (EPF) and is meant to strengthen the country’s defense capabilities. Moldova is the second-largest beneficiary of EU assistance provided through the EPF, after Ukraine. Thus, the total support provided to the country amounts to 317 million euros for the period 2021–2026. articles.title: Constitutional Court only partially grants Lelo's motion regarding examination of evidence during hearing
articles.summary: The Plenum of the Constitutional Court has only partially granted the motion filed by the political union of citizens Lelo – Strong Georgia regarding the examination of evidence during the hearing. The decision was communicated to the parties by the Chairman of the Constitutional Court, Revaz Nadaraia.
articles.body: The Plenum of the Constitutional Court has only partially granted the motion filed by the political union of citizens Lelo – Strong Georgia regarding the examination of evidence during the hearing. The decision was communicated to the parties by the Chairman of the Constitutional Court, Revaz Nadaraia. "The motion filed by the respondent party—the political union of citizens 'Lelo – Strong Georgia'—has been granted in part. The request to present every single internet link cited in the constitutional claim during the court proceedings is denied. Furthermore, the Court will not examine—during the hearing on the merits—facts that are 'generally known' (as per Article 31 of the Constitutional Court’s Regulations) or judicial acts that have already entered into legal force. During the course of the proceedings, the Court will assess the relevance of specific pieces of evidence cited in the claim—should their relevance be contested—either upon a substantiated motion from a party or on its own initiative. The ruling is final and is not subject to review or appeal. The Plenum was unanimous in adopting this ruling," stated Revaz Nadaraia. For context, "Lelo – Strong Georgia" had requested that an evidentiary hearing stage be conducted during the Constitutional Court’s proceedings regarding the lawsuit filed by "Georgian Dream" MPs, which seeks the banning of five opposition parties. This motion was submitted by Levan Samushia, representing the respondent side; however, representatives of other opposition parties also expressed their support for it.

articles.title: Hearings resume at Constitutional Court regarding potential ban of five opposition parties
articles.summary: The Constitutional Court has resumed hearings on a petition filed by Georgian Dream MPs seeking the banning of five opposition parties. The phase of the proceedings dedicated to opening statements and explanations has concluded; starting today, the Constitutional Court is moving on to the questioning stage.
articles.body: The Constitutional Court has resumed hearings on a petition filed by Georgian Dream MPs seeking the banning of five opposition parties. The phase of the proceedings dedicated to opening statements and explanations has concluded; starting today, the Constitutional Court is moving on to the questioning stage. As explained by the Chairman of the Constitutional Court, Revaz Nadaraia, the Court will first pose questions to the plaintiffs, followed by the respondents. For context, the Constitutional Court began reviewing the petition on October 21. The case is being heard by a plenum consisting of seven judges of the Constitutional Court. The petition submitted to the Constitutional Court is signed by 88 Members of Parliament. Based on their lawsuit, the court is set to consider the issue of declaring the following five political associations unconstitutional: "Unity – National Movement"; "Coalition for Change – Gvaramia, Melia, Girchi, Droa"; "Strong Georgia – Lelo, For the People, For Freedom!"; the "Federalist Party"; and the party "Gakharia for Georgia." The constitutional lawsuit is accompanied by the conclusion of a temporary investigative commission established within the 11th convocation of the Parliament.

Armenian opposition launches campaign against proposed constitutional changes
articles.summary: The opposition have dubbed potential amendments ‘Aliyev’s constitution’.
articles.body: Several major opposition groups have launched a public awareness campaign against proposed constitutional changes, saying they aim to ‘defend Armenia’s independence’ and prevent the adoption of what they call ‘Aliyev’s constitution’. The campaign began on Sunday, despite no agreement having been reached on holding a constitutional referendum. Amending Armenia’s constitution is an Azerbaijani precondition for signing a peace treaty, with Baku arguing that the Declaration of Independence, referenced in the constitution’s preamble, contains territorial claims against Azerbaijan. The two countries initialled a peace agreement in August 2025 but have yet to sign it. Despite winning the June parliamentary elections, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s Civil Contract party lacks the two-thirds majority required to call a referendum to amend the constitution and cannot pass a decision without the support of the opposition. The opposition has dubbed the proposed new constitution Azerbaijani President Ilham ‘Aliyev’s constitution’, arguing that the changes are being pursued to meet Azerbaijan’s demands. Even though the newly drafted constitution is yet to be published, the authorities already stated that the new draft makes no mention of the Declaration of Independence. The campaign began in Yerevan’s metro stations, where opposition figures headed in different directions across the city. They carried Armenian national flags and copies of the ballot papers used in the 1991 independence referendum. ‘We are launching public awareness campaigns in Yerevan related to the protection of independence’, Narek Karapetyan, head of the Strong Armenia faction in parliament, announced in the video shared on social media from the metro. ‘Yes to independence’, Armenia Alliance MP Christine Vardanyan is heard saying in the background. ‘This is not simply a matter of any particular article of the constitution; this is a question of independence and sovereignty’, Vardanyan said in a separate video. According to Vardanyan, the aim of the campaign is to explain to citizens the constitutional amendment process, which she said was being carried out at Azerbaijan’s demand. Armenian authorities also acknowledge that Azerbaijan has set this precondition, but maintain that they do not discuss potential amendments with foreign states. The government also says that constitutional reform has been on its agenda since shortly after it came to power in 2018. The campaign was agreed on at a meeting held a day earlier between representatives of several opposition groups and other public and political figures who, as they said, had responded to a call for ‘unity’. The meeting was part of a broader opposition initiative announced earlier in the week, when several major opposition groups declared the formation of a nationwide alliance against the proposed constitutional changes, among other issues. The alliance itself was announced shortly after the arrest of Russian–Armenian billionaire and Strong Armenia leader Samvel Karapetyan. They also called on other political parties, public figures, and civil society representatives to join the initiative. Strong Armenia claimed that the meeting had been planned before Samvel Karapetyan’s arrest, describing his detention as an attempt to hinder the opposition’s unity. ‘We are the defenders of our constitution, and the constitution is the defender of our independence. The Declaration of Independence is the foundation of our independence. And this is something that our people must decide. A significant part of our political parties have already made that decision’, Narek Karapetyan said in a press briefing following the meeting on 7 November. He also said that the opposition would participate in street protests if it deems it necessary, expressing hope that the public would join the protests. ‘We are prepared to use all available means to defend the constitution’, Karapetyan added. The initiative was met with criticism from the ruling Civil Contract party. Parliamentary Speaker Ruben Rubinyan accused Armenia’s former presidents Levon Ter-Petrosyan, Robert Kocharyan, and Serzh Sargsyan, whose political parties and alliances joined the consolidation, of having undermined the country’s independence. ‘Levon Ter-Petrosyan, Robert Kocharyan, and Serzh Sargsyan have been and continue to be the main enemies of Armenia’s independence. Their political heirs spare no effort in fighting against Armenia’s independence and serving their masters in Kaluga. The Kaluga mercenaries will be defeated by an independent Armenia’, Rubinyan wrote on Facebook. Pashinyan and his party often call Samvel Karapetyan the ‘Kaluga oligarch’, in reference to the Russian city where he began building his business empire. Rubinyan’s deputy, Vahagn Aleksanyan, also mocked the opposition campaign, referring to its participants as Soviet-era KGB agents. ‘One day, the KGB agents come out to fight for independence’, Aleksanyan wrote , claiming that the campaign was intended to ‘defend the looting of citizens carried out by Electric Networks of Armenia (ENA)’. The remarks appeared to refer to the recent criminal investigation into alleged damages of more than ֏65 billion ($180 million) at the ENA, which is owned by Samvel Karapetyan’s Tashir Group but is currently under state management pending nationalisation. Rubinyan also said that, in a strange twist of fate, the political forces now opposing a constitutional referendum were the same ones that had previously rigged all three constitutional referendums held in Armenia. He was referring to the referendums held in 1995, 2005, and 2015, which he accused Ter-Petrosyan, Kocharyan, and Sargsyan of rigging. She is also a strong advocate for media literacy and closely follows Armenia’s media landscape.

Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi to report to Putin based on talks’ progress — Kremlin
articles.summary: Russian Presidential Aide Vladimir Medinsky leads the Russian delegation
articles.body: MOSCOW, November 10. /TASS/. The Russian delegation, which is currently participating in trilateral negotiations with the United States and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi, will decide whether to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin in a "telegraphic" mode or provide a comprehensive report, depending on how the talks proceed, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday. "The delegation will be making decisions depending on how the negotiations proceed," Peskov said at a news briefing. Talks between Russia, the United States and Ukraine on a Ukrainian settlement are held on November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi. Russian Presidential Aide Vladimir Medinsky leads the Russian delegation, while Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov heads Ukraine’s team. Kremlin Spokesman Peskov stated earlier the negotiations would focus on security guarantees. The two-day talks began on Tuesday at about 8:15 a.m. GMT. The Russian and Ukrainian delegations are seated opposite each other at a U-shaped table.
